messages:
Alex: quick follow-up to the autoscale RFC — thinking about elastic shard resizing (adjust vGPU->shard mapping in-place) instead of always spinning new pool nodes. idea: avoid tenant re-placement and long startup latencies by changing shard sizes on existing machines.
Marta: curious — how do you handle fragmentation? shrinking a shard could leave unusable GPU memory. :thinking:
Jamie: qm: quantized models and large KV caches need warmup. in-place change might still force full KV reinit for some tenants. we need a migration step.
Ravi: metric-wise, what's the trigger? queued_requests alone will oscillate. maybe use a composite: queued + p99-latency + sustained-utilization(window=5m).
Chen: +1 to composite. also add a cost signal so we don't scale up for short noisy spikes. cooldowns and step-sizing matter.
Priya: safety concern — live-serving migrations can surface errors. we must guarantee no request loss and clear rollback plan. draining semantics need to be explicit.
Alex: proposal sketch: two ops — `soft-resize` (adjust capacity annotation, gradual slot drain, keep old shard until warmup) and `hard-resize` (evict & reassign). default to `soft-resize` with max 1 slot migration concurrently per host.
Alex: sample controller config idea:
```
shardResize:
  min_shard: 1
  max_shard: 8
  step: 1
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  concurrent_migrations_per_host: 1
  warmup_grace: 60   # seconds to keep both KVs alive
```
Jamie: example drain command we can expose to tenants: `redwoodctl shard drain --shard-id=sh-123 --timeout=120s` — returns slot state and remaining inflight.
Chen: instrumentation we should add: `shard.resize_attempts`, `shard.resize_success`, `placement.move_latency_ms`, `gpu.fragmentation_bytes`. make them high-cardinality tagged by pool and shard-size.
Ravi: tradeoff note: in-place resizing reduces placement churn but increases fragmentation. need periodic compaction job that recombines small shards when global slack exists.
Marta: operator complexity is real. suggest a staged rollout: 1) enable soft-resize dry-run (controller emits decisions but doesn't act), 2) canary a single pool with non-critical workloads, 3) expand.
Priya: add a kill-switch label `redwood.dev/resize-enabled=false` so customers can opt-out during initial rollout. also require an SLA gating check before resize (no resize if tenant has >X p99 errors last 1h).
Alex: agreed. experiment plan: run dry-run for 48h, compare placement moves, avg-p50 latency, and cost-per-token. if compaction job is needed, run weekly and measure reclaimed capacity.
Jamie: small nit — make warmup_kv optional per-model. some models can share caches, others can't. controller should read model capabilities from catalog.
Chen: I'll draft the metrics dashboard (per-pool: resize rate, success ratio, avg migration time) and a compaction job spec.
Ravi: I'll prototype the composite trigger and a hysteresis filter to reduce oscillation.
Marta: ops checklist: RBAC for resize, rollout doc, and runbook for migration failures. I'll owner the runbook.
ops-bot: Deploybot: canary controller image pushed: redwood/controller:v2.12-canary (not enabled). :rocket:
Priya: thanks — next meeting to review dry-run results in 1 week. :+1:
